raw.rationale: A lipid peroxidase inhibitor (e.g., ferrostatin-class) is expected to rescue cells from ferroptosis rather than kill them, so at 2.5 µM it is unlikely to show selective cytotoxicity; PRISM single-concentration data for such compounds typically show few or no lineage-selective kills, with any apparent selectivity driven by lineage-specific ferroptosis sensitivity (e.g., high PUFA/iron, low GPX4) rather than the compound's own mechanism.
